purpose: Structured, non-authoritative human review worksheet for one exact pending Shine Defence candidate.
candidateBinding: The checklist binds to one exact candidate id, app id, repository, release commit, Defence-profile path/blob/version and policy list.
The checklist also pins the canonical Defence registry version and Git blob SHA used to derive its policy requirements.
A checklist never changes candidate status or grants a badge.

itemStates.meaning: No human conclusion has been recorded for this requirement.
A human reviewer explicitly concluded the requirement is satisfied for the exact candidate release.
A human reviewer explicitly concluded the requirement is not satisfied for the exact candidate release.

humanAuthorization.rule: Only an explicit approved human attestation may authorize first certification or re-certification. Generator output is always pending.

rules: Checklist requirements are derived from the exact canonical artefacts claimed by the candidate.
JSON artefacts with a requirements array produce one checklist item per requirement.
Canonical artefacts without a requirements array produce one artefact-integrity checklist item rather than being silently treated as reviewed.
Candidate evidence is copied as reference material but is not automatically mapped to requirements or treated as sufficient.
A satisfied item must cite at least one candidate evidence id or contain a non-empty human reviewer note.
Approval requires every checklist item to be satisfied, a bounded reviewer id, an ISO reviewedAt timestamp, and a bounded human summary.
Rejection requires at least one not_satisfied item and explicit human reviewer metadata.
Pending authorization cannot contain a reviewer identity, reviewedAt timestamp or approval/rejection summary.
Acceptance helpers must independently validate the approved checklist against the current candidate and canonical registry before they may create an accepted decision.
nonClaims: A generated checklist is not a security review.
Checklist approval is a human attestation recorded by the repository; it is not cryptographic proof of real-world identity.
A satisfied checklist does not prove software is invulnerable.
The checklist does not replace app-specific tests, code review or release verification.
